page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources are provisioned via dedicated allocation, providing 8 physical cores with two threads per core to deliver a total of 16 vCPUs.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, resulting in an allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per compute unit. This server profile does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators and features no integrated local NVMe storage, meaning persistent storage requirements must be fulfilled through external network-attached volumes. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external routing and remote administration.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a balanced hardware configuration suitable for steady enterprise execution. Because local scratch storage is omitted, workloads requiring high sustained I/O depend entirely on remote block volumes. The dedicated compute allocation and high processor clock rate position this instance well for web application hosting, build systems, microservices backends, and containerized enterprise services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.8-64 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4.0 GB per-core allocation profile. The instance contains zero GPUs and does not incorporate bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage needs. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Operating without local scratch drives, the system trades off high-speed local disk I/O in exchange for flexible volume attachments. The configuration is appropriate for general enterprise workloads, application backends, container orchestration nodes, and distributed compilation pipelines requiring consistent CPU performance.
